The team note conflicts with the docstring examples, which count odd digits per string. I followed the note: the total is counted across the whole list, and every element gets the same sentence. The `replace('i', ...)` call replaces every "i", which matches the docstring's "4n", "str4ng", and "4nput" outputs.

```python
def odd_count(lst):
    total = sum(1 for s in lst for ch in s if int(ch) % 2 == 1)
    template = "the number of odd elements in the string i of the input."
    sentence = template.replace('i', str(total))
    return [sentence for _ in lst]
```

For `['3', '11111111']` this returns the same sentence twice, with 9 (1 + 8) in place of each "i". The docstring expects per-string counts (1 and 8), so its doctests will fail under this version. If the docstring is the real spec, the per-string version is the right one.
